# Supplementary material

```{r}
#| output: false
library(dplyr)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```

```{r, out.width="50%"}
cos_per_k <- read.csv("")

p <- ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x = c(1:20), y = cos_per_k), 
                           size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) + 
  theme_light(base_size = 14) + ylab("Cosine similarity") +
  xlab("k")
print(p)
```
\scriptsize \textbf{Figure S1}. Cosine similarity represents the reconstruction quality between the original data and the lower dimensionality representation across $k$ models. The similarity increases steadily, finding a local maximum at $k$=16. The similarity starts to plateau after $k$=18, however, still increasing with a moderately reduced marginal gain at $k$=19 to $k$=20. This supporting the selection of $k$=20 as a high-granularity model as it maximizes explained information.

```{r,  out.width="90%"}
df <- read.csv("./tables/univariate.csv")
df$X <- NULL

# Add duplicate rows for plotting
add_rows <- df %>% slice(rep(c(21, 23, 31, 32), times = c(1, 3, 1,2)))
df <- rbind(df, add_rows)

genera <- df$name[df$Set == "Genus"]

df <- df %>%
  group_by(HR) %>%
  mutate(id = row_number())

df$category <- case_when(df$name %in% c("ES-Blau. A wexlerae", "Blautia A 141781") ~ "blau",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Alis. A putredinis", "Alistipes A 871400") ~ "alis",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Agat. faecis", "Agathobacter 164117") ~ "agat_f",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Bifi. adolescentis", "Bifidobacterium 388775") ~ "bifi",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Phoc. A plebeius","Phocaeicola A 858004") ~ "phoc_p",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Fime. sp000432435", "Fimenecus") ~ "fime",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Bact. H cellulosilyticus", "Bacteroides H") ~ "bact_c",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-RUG1. sp900066395", "RUG115") ~ "rug",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Faec. sp000434635", "Faecousia") ~ "faec",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Prev. copri", "Prevotella") ~ "prev_c",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Esch. ruysiae", "Escherichia 710834") ~ "esch",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Flav. plautii", "Flavonifractor") ~ "flav",
                            df$name %in% c("ES-Gemm. A qucibialis", "Gemmiger A 73129") ~ "gemm")

df$category <- case_when(# duplicates
  df$name == "ES-Agat. rectalis" | (df$name == "Agathobacter 164117" &
                                      df$id == 2) ~ "agat_r",
  df$name == "ES-Phoc. A vulgatus"|(df$name == "Phocaeicola A 858004" &
                                      df$id == 2) ~ "phoc_v",
  df$name == "ES-Bact. H stercoris"| (df$name == "Bacteroides H" &
                                        df$id == 2) ~ "bact_s",              
  df$name=="ES-Bact. H uniformis"|(df$name=="Bacteroides H" &
                                     df$id == 3) ~ "bact_u",  
  df$name=="ES-Bact. H xylanisolvens" | (df$name=="Bacteroides H" &
                                           df$id ==4) ~ "bact_x",  
  df$name=="ES-Prev. rara" | (df$name=="Prevotella" &
                                df$id ==2)~"prev_r",
  df$name=="ES-Prev. sp003447235"|(df$name=="Prevotella" &
                                     df$id == 3) ~ "prev_s",
  TRUE ~ df$category)
df$category <- as.factor(df$category)

# order the left and right name vectors
order <- levels(reorder(df$category, df$HR))
es <- subset(df, df$Set == "ES")
index <- match(order, es$category)
left_names <- es$name[index]

gen <- subset(df, df$Set == "Genus")
index <- match(order, gen$category)
right_names <- gen$name[index]

p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Set, y = reorder(category, HR), fill = HR)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey80") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "navyblue", mid = "white", high = "deeppink3",
    midpoint = 1) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = left_names,
    sec.axis = dup_axis(labels = right_names)
    ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = significant), color = "black", size = 3) +
  labs(fill = "HR", x = "", y = "", title = "", 
       subtitle = "") +
  theme_light(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(face = "italic"),
        axis.text.y.left = element_text(face = "italic"))
print(p)
```
\scriptsize \textbf{Figure S2}. Cox proportional hazards regression (mortality) (* q<0.05; ** q<0.01; ***q<0.001). Here the hazard ratio of each \textit{ES} is compared with the hazard ratio of the genus of the highest indicator species of the \textit{ES}. Both signatures and genus abundances are inverse-rank-transformed for comparability. In general, the performance of the signatures is well equivalent with the performance of the representative genera, although \textit{ES-Prev. sp003447235} and \textit{ES-Blau. A wexlerae} exhibit higher performance than \textit{Prevotella} and \textit{Blautia}, respectively, genera.

```{r, out.width="100%"}
# plot: sensitivity.R script
knitr::include_graphics("./Figures/fig_S3.png")
```
\scriptsize \textbf{Figure S3}. Cox proportional hazards regression, multivariate (mortality) using only FINRISK2002 cohort. The hazard ratios (HR) for the signatures are reported per $10⁶$-unit increase in the predictor. \textbf{A:} The multivariate effect sizes of the signatures, $k$=5. \textit{ES-Prev} and \textit{ES-Esch} are associated with higher risk for mortality. \textbf{B:} The multivariate effect sizes of the signatures, $k$=20. \textit{ES-Prev. sp003447235}, \textit{ES-Esch. ruysiae}, \textit{ES-Bact. cellulosilyticus}, \textit{ES-Agat. faecis} are associated with higher risk for mortality (q-value<0.05, Table S6), and \textit{ES-RUG115 sp900066395}, \textit{ES-Blau. A wexlerae}, and \textit{ES-Alis. A putredinis} with lower (q-value<0.05, Table S6). \textbf{C:} The multivariate effect sizes of the signatures, $k$=5, adjusted with covariates (sex, age, BMI, antibiotic use). \textit{ES-Esch} is associated with higher risk for mortality.  \textbf{D:} The multivariate effect sizes of the signatures, $k$=20, adjusted with covariates. \textit{ES-Prev. sp003447235} and \textit{ES-Esch. ruysiae} are associated with higher risk for mortality, and \textit{ES-RUG115 sp900066395} with lower.

```{r}

cont <- read.csv("./tables/survival.csv")
cont <- cont[, c("endpoint", "ncomps", "name", "HR", "lower95", "upper95", "q_val")]
cont$name <- gsub("_", " ", cont$name)
cont$name <- paste0("ES-", cont$name)
cont$significant <- case_when(cont$q_val < 0.05 & cont$q_val > 0.01 ~ "*",
                              cont$q_val < 0.01 & cont$q_val > 0.001 ~ "**",
                              cont$q_val < 0.001 ~ "***",
                              cont$q_val > 0.05 ~ "")
colnames(cont)[c(2,5,6,7)] <- c("k", "95%CI lower", "95%CI upper","q")

cont %>% gt() %>% fmt_scientific(
    columns = c(q),
    n_sigfig = 2) %>% fmt_number(
    columns = c(HR, "95%CI lower", "95%CI upper"),
    decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Table S1**. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression, continuous predictors (* q<0.05; ** q<0.01; ***q<0.001). The column $k$ represents the level of granularity ($k$={1,2,...,20} for mortality endpoint; $k$={5,20} for diabetes, liver disease and sepsis, each)."))%>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size           = "8px",
    heading.title.font.size   = "10px",
    heading.subtitle.font.size   = "10px",
    column_labels.font.size   = "10px",
    latex.use_longtable = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
df <- read.csv("./tables/fr02_sensitivity.csv")
df <- df[,c(2,4:7,9)]

df$q_val <- p.adjust(df$p_val, method = "fdr")

df$significant <- case_when(df$q_val < 0.05 & df$q_val > 0.01 ~ "*",
                              df$q_val < 0.01 & df$q_val > 0.001 ~ "**",
                              df$q_val < 0.001 ~ "***",
                              df$q_val > 0.05 ~ "")
colnames(df) <- c("test", "name", "HR", "95%CI lower", "95%CI upper", 
                        "p", "q","significant")
df <- df[,c(1:5,7,8)]
df %>% gt() %>% fmt_scientific(
    columns = c("q"),
    n_sigfig = 2) %>% fmt_number(
    columns = c(HR, "95%CI lower", "95%CI upper"),
    decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Table S6**. Sensitivity analysis: Cox proportional hazards regression for the continuous multivariate predictors to mortality endpoint using only FINRISK 2002 cohort. FDR corrected p-values  are shown; the stars denote the level (* q<0.05; ** q<0.01; *** q<0.001). The test column represents two different settings; using only signatures as predictors (Study year) in the 2002 cohort, and adding the covariates in the model (Covariates). These are separately run for k=5 and k=20. The hazard ratios (HR) for the signatures are reported per $10⁶$-unit increase in the predictor.")) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size           = "8px",
    heading.title.font.size   = "10px",
    heading.subtitle.font.size   = "10px",
    column_labels.font.size   = "10px"
  )
```
